findings.location: migrations/120_ownerless_tenant_zero_unarm.sql B1 (role_assignment DELETE) — verified live against a hand-crafted fixture, ROLLBACK-safe temp databases, not covered by ci/checks/db/migration-120-ownerless-unarm.test.ts
findings.issue: B1's DELETE predicate discriminates 'was this row produced by migration 118' using ONLY `ra.source = 'backfill'`. It does NOT also require `ra.confirmed_by = 'backfill'` (B2, the grant DELETE, DOES use confirmed_by as its sole marker — an intentional asymmetry, or an oversight, is unclear from the ADR). `role_assignment.source` is a client-controlled, unconstrained free-text column: POST /api/role-assignments (src/http/grants.ts:1094-1097) reads `source` directly from the request body with only a `typeof === 'string'` check, no CHECK constraint/enum in the schema (independently confirmed by the pre-existing test ci/checks/db/role-assignment.test.ts:392, 'arbitrary non-empty source string accepted (no CHECK enum)'). `confirmed_by`, by contrast, is ALWAYS server-derived from the authenticated actor (R-AUTH, grants.ts:1104-1106/1157-1171) and can never be set to a client-chosen literal via the production JWT-auth path. CONSTRUCTED AND VERIFIED LIVE (independent adversarial probe, not part of the coder's test suite): a role_assignment row with `employee_id`=assistant-agent, `role_id`=role-configurator, `confirmed_by`=a real authenticated actor's employee id, `source`='backfill' (simulating a legitimate admin who happened to pass that literal string in a POST body) is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a migration-118-produced row to B1's predicate and IS deleted by migration 120 if the tenant has no confirmed tenant-owner assignment at that moment. This is a genuine marker-precision gap in B1 specifically (B2/grant is NOT exposed to this vector, since grant.confirmed_by can never be client-set to 'backfill' through the live write path).
findings.suggestion: Not blocking for THIS task, for three converging reasons verified independently: (1) reaching the vulnerable state requires an ALREADY-ownerless tenant (per this task's own established fact, and T-0573's, ownerless tenants are exclusively test/fixture orphans or manual DB tampering — never a live registerTenant() outcome) that ALSO has an actor holding a delegable admin grant able to pass validateAdminDelegation's non-owner assignment gate (itself only reachable if a constructor-admin/equivalent was assigned while an owner still existed, i.e. requires the SAME owner-removed-after-the-fact precondition as R-2/R-3 below); (2) the blast radius of an over-deletion here is bounded to exactly the same role_assignment migration 118 itself would have produced (agent->role-configurator) — it does not let an attacker delete an arbitrary OTHER grant, since the rest of B1's WHERE clause (cfg_role.slug/agent.slug/agent.kind) still pins the row shape tightly; (3) the underlying looseness (source has no CHECK/enum) is a pre-existing property of the role_assignment table predating T-0573/T-0594, not introduced by this task — T-0594 merely elevates its consequence by being the first consumer to treat `source` as a security-relevant discriminator for a DELETE. Recommend a fast follow-up (new task, not T-0594): either add `AND ra.confirmed_by = 'backfill'` to B1 (this WOULD be a body-diff-only fix to an unmerged migration, still safe to edit since 120 has not shipped to any stand yet, unlike 118) for defense-in-depth symmetry with B2, or add a CHECK constraint / enum on role_assignment.source in a future migration. Non-blocking because migration 120 has not yet been applied anywhere (dev-only worktree, per pr-handoff's own docker-compose teardown discipline) — a same-branch tightening of B1 before promotion is strictly better than blocking, and I recommend it as a suggestion, not a gate, since the realistic exploit chain requires an already-broken ownerless-tenant state that is out of scope for both this migration and its predecessor by the same standing argument the ADR itself uses for R-2's overall non-blocking disposition.

findings.location: migrations/120_ownerless_tenant_zero_unarm.sql B1 scope (role_assignment DELETE, agent-only) — verified live via raw psql against a hand-crafted 'owner existed at 118-time, then removed' fixture, not enumerated in SPEC/ADR as a distinct state from the T_OWNERLESS fixture
findings.issue: Migration 120's B1 block is scoped, by its own WHERE clause (`agent.slug = 'assistant-agent' AND agent.kind = 'agent'`), to delete ONLY the assistant-agent -> role-configurator role_assignment. It structurally cannot and does not touch a HUMAN's role-configurator role_assignment. CONSTRUCTED AND VERIFIED LIVE: seeded a tenant where a real owner existed when migration 118 ran (so A4 legitimately inserted an owner -> role-configurator row, source/confirmed_by/granted_by='backfill', same marker as A5/A6/A7), then manually deleted the owner's tenant-owner role_assignment (simulating an operator mistake or a race between 118 and 120's apply-times — exactly the race scenario named in the task brief). Running migration 120 against this tenant correctly deletes the assistant-agent role_assignment and all 4 grants (0 remaining) but LEAVES THE FORMER-OWNER'S role-configurator role_assignment FULLY INTACT (1 row, confirmed_by IS NOT NULL) — this human can still exercise role-configurator's authoring_draft/llm_connection:configure/system_agent:operate capabilities in a tenant that migration 120 has just certified/left as 'ownerless'. This state (owner existed at 118-apply-time, removed before 120-apply-time) is NOT one of the three fixtures (T_FULL/T_PARTIAL/T_OWNERLESS) enumerated in SPEC §7 AC-1 or the ADR's rejected-alternatives table — it is a genuinely distinct case the spec's own three-tenant taxonomy does not cover.
findings.suggestion: Not blocking, verified live: re-ran migration 118's own AC-1 invariant predicate (verbatim SQL, unedited) against this exact post-race, post-120 tenant state and confirmed it STILL FLAGS the tenant (1 violation) — the owner_ra JOIN inside AC-1's role_assignment branch requires the assignee to itself hold a confirmed tenant-owner assignment, which no longer exists, so the predicate's NOT EXISTS branch fires correctly. This means the exact same 'not a silent hole, AC-1 monitoring will catch it' argument the ADR/T-0573-review already relies on for the R-2 (agent-armament) case applies equally to this human-role_assignment case — the dangling grant is undetected by migration 120 itself but IS detected by the existing, unmodified observability the ADR leans on. Scope is arguably correct as designed (F3/O4 in the spec explicitly reserve 'a human's role-configurator assignment' as never-migration-120's-concern — the spec frames 120 as unarming ONLY the agent-reachable circuit, not general role-configurator hygiene for humans who cease to be the owner), but the ADR's own argument table (§2, 'Владелец появится позже') and rejected-alternatives section do not explicitly discuss the SYMMETRIC case (owner DISAPPEARS after having been armed) — worth a one-line acknowledgment in a future ADR revision, not a code change to this migration.
